newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian state clears Easdaq rules - paper.
newsitem.headline: Belgian state clears Easdaq rules - paper.

text.p: The Belgian government has published its authorisation for the Easdaq European small cap market in the state's official journal, Belgian financial newspaper L'Echo reported on Tuesday.
The publication lifts an administrative barrier that had stood in the way of the market's first listings.
Easdaq's electronic screen based trading system was ready for launch on September 30, but no trading has yet taken place because of the lack of listings.
However, the exchange is confident there will be 10 to 15 stocks quoted before the end of 1996.
Easdaq, or European Association of Securities Dealers Automated Quotation, aims to plug a hole in Europe's financial markets, making venture capital accessible to small growing companies.

It is modelled on the U.S.'s successful Nasdaq market. Nasdaq is one of Easdaq's shareholders and, initially, it is foreseen that Easdaq's first listings will be by European companies already traded on Nasdaq.
